newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bildt, in Moscow, criticises Serbian leadership.
newsitem.headline: Bildt, in Moscow, criticises Serbian leadership.

text.p: International peace coordinator Carl Bildt renewed criticism of Serbia's leadership on Monday after talks with Russian officials, Itar-Tass news agency said.

The actions of Serbia's leadership have become "a source of serious unease in the international community," Tass quoted Bildt as saying after talks in Moscow with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.

Bildt, the international community's High Representative in Bosnia, has stepped up criticism of the Serbian authorities since the government threatened a crackdown to stop huge street demonstrations in Belgrade against President Slobodan Milosevic.
Russia has traditional ties with its fellow Orthodox Christian Slavs in Serbia.
Western diplomats at a European security summit in Lisbon last week said Russia had been responsible for a call for Serbian democracy being struck out of a final summit declaration.
Bildt also told reporters that Russia was "an important, central" factor in bringing about peace in the region.
He held out hope that Russian forces would continue to participate in international peacekeeping forces for another year or 18 months, Tass said.
